1. Juvenile xanthogranuloma — common congenital/early-childhood yellow/orange papules or nodules on trunk/head that often spontaneously involute; fits having a few lesions present since birth with some resolving.
2. Nevus simplex (salmon patch/stork bite) — flat pink patches present at birth that frequently fade during childhood; plausible given spontaneous resolution.
3. Infantile hemangioma — vascular red/blue lesions that often appear in infancy and can involute over time; would blanch with pressure and be raised during proliferative phase.
4. Congenital melanocytic nevus — pigmented lesions present at birth (usually brown/tan, persistent); less likely to resolve but still possible for small/medium lesions.
5. Cutaneous mastocytosis (urticaria pigmentosa) — brown/tan macules from infancy that may itch and can show a positive Darier sign; can improve with age.

Recommended next steps (to confirm/rule out): focused skin exam noting color (yellow/tan/red/pink), surface (flat vs raised), blanching with pressure, palpation firmness, and testing for Darier sign; consider dermoscopy and photographic documentation. If uncertainty persists or lesions are nodular/atypical, arrange dermatology referral and consider biopsy (histology) or ultrasound for suspected hemangioma.
